items.title: The Riemann curvature operator and the derived Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.
items.strategy: Define the curvature operator R(X,Y)Z = nabla_X nabla_Y Z - nabla_Y nabla_X Z - nabla_{[X,Y]} Z, its chart components, and the lowered Riemann, Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors by metric contraction, with the sign and index conventions fixed and certified by the tensoriality theorem.

items.title: Tensoriality of the curvature, its coordinate formula and its point-normal metric formula
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

**(c) Point-normal formula.** If the chart is point-normal at $p$, that is
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]), then, writing
$g_{ad,bc}:=\partial_b\partial_cg_{ad}$,
$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.
items.strategy: Prove that the curvature operator is a smooth (1,3)-tensor field, derive the chart formula for its components, and derive the point-normal four-term formula for the lowered components.

items.title: The algebraic symmetries of the curvature tensor and the symmetry of the Ricci and Einstein tensors
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be as in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Then the following
identities hold for all indices $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ and at every point of
every smooth chart:

**(a) Skew-symmetries.** $R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}$ and $R_{abcd}=-R_{abdc}$.
Equivalently, for smooth vector fields,
$$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(X,Y)W,Z\bigr) \quad\text{and}\quad g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=-g\bigl(R(Y,X)Z,W\bigr).$$

**(b) Exchange of the index pairs.** $R_{abcd}=R_{cdab}$, equivalently
$g\bigl(R(X,Y)Z,W\bigr)=g\bigl(R(Z,W)X,Y\bigr)$.

**(c) First Bianchi identity.** $R_{a[bcd]}=0$, that is,
$$R_{abcd}+R_{acdb}+R_{adbc}=0 .$$

**(d) Ricci symmetry.** $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ba}$;
consequently the Einstein tensor is symmetric, $G_{ab}=G_{ba}$.
items.strategy: Derive the two skew-symmetries, the exchange of the index pairs, the first Bianchi identity and the Ricci and Einstein symmetries in a point-normal chart from the four-term metric formula and the commutation of mixed partials.

items.title: The second Bianchi identity and the vanishing divergence of the Einstein tensor
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be as in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Write $;e$ for the induced
covariant derivative and raise indices with $g^{-1}$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]] clause (c),
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Second Bianchi identity.** For all indices $a,b,c,d,e$,
$$R^a{}_{bcd;e}+R^a{}_{bde;c}+R^a{}_{bec;d}=0,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad R_{abcd;e}+R_{abde;c}+R_{abec;d}=0 .$$
Equivalently, the antisymmetrization over the last three slots vanishes:
$R^a{}_{b[cd;e]}=0$.

**(b) Contracted identities.** $\nabla^a\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}
=\tfrac12\nabla_bS$, and consequently
$$\nabla^aG_{ab}=0\qquad\text{for every }b,$$
where $\nabla^aG_{ab}:=g^{ae}\nabla_eG_{ab}$. The conclusion is the vanishing
of the contracted divergence for each second index; it does not assert that
all components $\nabla_cG_{ab}$ vanish.
items.strategy: Prove the second Bianchi identity in chart components and contract it twice, first to nabla^a Ric_ab = (1/2) nabla_b S and then to the divergence-free Einstein tensor.

items.title: Jacobi fields, geodesic variations and conjugate instants along a geodesic
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$ be its curvature ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior
([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be an affinely parametrized
geodesic with $D_s\gamma'=0$, written $T:=\gamma'$
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]); the parameter is the affinely
parametrized one of that definition and need not be proper time.

**(a) Fields along $\gamma$ and the derivative $D_s$.** A **field along
$\gamma$** is a section $J$ of the pullback bundle $\gamma^*TM$, and $D_s$
denotes the covariant derivative along $\gamma$ of
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]. A field is **smooth** when its
coefficients in a smooth local frame of $M$ around each point of $\gamma$ are
$C^\infty$ on the corresponding parameter interval. At an included endpoint
of $I$ all derivatives below are one-sided.

**(b) Jacobi field.** A **Jacobi field along $\gamma$** is a smooth field $J$
along $\gamma$ satisfying the **Jacobi equation**
$$D_s^2J=R(T,J)T\qquad(s\in I),$$
that is $D_s^2J=R(\gamma',J)\gamma'$. The assignment
$J\mapsto R(T,J)T$, which associates with a field along $\gamma$ another
field along $\gamma$ and is $\mathbb R$-linear, is the **Jacobi operator of
$\gamma$**. Whether the field is smooth only piecewise is stated whenever a
statement uses piecewise fields; the unqualified term means globally smooth.

**(c) Geodesic variations.** A **geodesic variation with affine
parameter $s$** is a smooth map $F:J_0\times I\to M$, where
$J_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an open interval with nonempty interior, such that
for every $r\in J_0$ the curve $s\mapsto F(r,s)$ is a geodesic with affine
parameter $s$. Its **variation field** is the field $s\mapsto\partial_rF(r,s)$
along the curve $s\mapsto F(0,s)$. The variation field of a geodesic
variation is a Jacobi field along that curve
([[thm-gr-jacobi-equation-and-geodesic-deviation]] clause (c)).

**(d) Conjugate instants and multiplicity.** Let $s_0<s_1$ be points of $I$.
The event $\gamma(s_1)$ is **conjugate to** $\gamma(s_0)$ **along $\gamma$**
when there is a nonzero Jacobi field $J$ along $\gamma$ with
$J(s_0)=J(s_1)=0$. In that case $s_1$ is called a **conjugate instant** of
$\gamma$ (with respect to $s_0$, when the base point needs to be named), and
the **multiplicity** of the conjugate instant is the dimension of the real
vector space of Jacobi fields vanishing at $s_0$ and $s_1$; the fields
vanishing at $s_0$ form a $4$-dimensional space and the multiplicity is at
most $4$, since a Jacobi field is determined by its value and derivative at
$s_0$ ([[thm-gr-jacobi-equation-and-geodesic-deviation]] clause (d)). For a
geodesic with $\gamma(s_0)=p$ and $\gamma'(s_0)=v$, the corresponding
possibility of conjugacy is measured by the derivative of the exponential
map at $s_1v$
([[lem-gr-conjugacy-via-the-exponential-map]]); that equivalence is proved,
not assumed here. No conjugate instant is asserted to exist.

**(e) The normal bundle.** If $\gamma$ is future timelike with
$g(T,T)=-1$, define its **normal bundle** to be the vector subbundle
$$N_\gamma:=\bigsqcup_{s\in I}N_\gamma(s)\subseteq\gamma^*TM,\qquad N_\gamma(s):=\{v\in T_{\gamma(s)}M:g_{\gamma(s)}(v,T(s))=0\}.$$
A **normal field** is a smooth section $J$ of $N_\gamma$, equivalently a
smooth field along $\gamma$ satisfying $g(J,T)=0$. Each fibre $N_\gamma(s)$
has dimension three, the restriction of $g_{\gamma(s)}$ to it is positive
definite, and $D_s$ maps normal fields to normal fields, since
$\frac{d}{ds}g(J,T)=g(D_sJ,T)+g(J,D_sT)=g(D_sJ,T)$ and $D_sT=0$; these
facts are proved in [[lem-gr-normal-index-form-factorization]] clause (b).
The norm of a normal field is $|J(s)|:=\sqrt{g_{\gamma(s)}(J(s),J(s))}$.
For any field $V$ along $\gamma$, its **normal component** is the field
$$V^\perp(s):=V(s)+g_{\gamma(s)}(V(s),T(s))\,T(s).$$
Indeed $g(T,T)=-1$ implies $g(V^\perp,T)=0$ and
$V=V^\perp-g(V,T)T$.
items.strategy: Define Jacobi fields along an affinely parametrized geodesic by D_s^2 J = R(T,J)T, geodesic variations with their variation fields, conjugate instants with multiplicity, and the normal bundle of a unit timelike geodesic.

items.title: The Jacobi equation, geodesic deviation and the initial-value theory of Jacobi fields
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $R$ be its
curvature ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let
$I,J_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be intervals with nonempty interior
([[def-interval]]), and let $F:J_0\times I\to M$ be a smooth map. Write
$T:=\partial_tF$ and $J^F:=\partial_rF$; a field along $F$ means a smooth
section of $F^*TM$ over $J_0\times I$, and $D_r,D_t$ are the covariant
derivatives in the two parameters
([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Curvature as the commutator of the two derivatives.** For every smooth
field $V$ along $F$,
$$\bigl(D_tD_r-D_rD_t\bigr)V=R(T,J^F)V .$$

**(b) Geodesic deviation.** Suppose in addition that for every $r\in J_0$ the
curve $t\mapsto F(r,t)$ is a geodesic with affine parameter $t$, that is
$D_tT=0$. Then $D_tJ^F=D_rT$ and
$$D_t^2J^F=R(T,J^F)T .$$
Consequently, for every $r$ the field $t\mapsto J^F(r,t)$ is a Jacobi field
along the geodesic $t\mapsto F(r,t)$
([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (b)), and for a geodesic
variation the variation field is a Jacobi field.

**(c) Initial data.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a smooth geodesic and let
$s_0\in I$. For every pair $J_0,J_1\in T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$ there exists exactly
one smooth Jacobi field $J$ along $\gamma$ with
$$J(s_0)=J_0,\qquad D_sJ(s_0)=J_1 .$$
The set of all Jacobi fields along $\gamma$ is a real vector space of
dimension $8$, and $J\mapsto\bigl(J(s_0),D_sJ(s_0)\bigr)$ is a linear
isomorphism onto $T_{\gamma(s_0)}M\oplus T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$.

**(d) The tangential component.** Let $\gamma$ be a smooth geodesic and $J$ a
smooth Jacobi field along it. Then $s\mapsto g(J,\gamma')(s)$ is affine, and
if $\gamma$ is future timelike with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-1$, the normal
component $J^\perp$ of [[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause
(e), explicitly $J^\perp=J+g(J,\gamma')\gamma'$, is again a Jacobi field
along $\gamma$.
items.strategy: Compute the commutator of the two covariant derivatives along a two-parameter map, derive the geodesic deviation equation, and prove that initial value and derivative determine a Jacobi field uniquely on an eight-dimensional space.

items.title: The differential of the exponential map and conjugacy along a geodesic
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $p\in M$,
let $\mathcal E_p\subseteq T_pM$ be the exponential domain and
$\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$ the exponential map of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]], and identify
$T_{h}(T_pM)$ with $T_pM$ by the canonical isomorphism for every
$h\in T_pM$ ([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]).

**(a) The differential in terms of Jacobi fields.** Let $v\in T_pM$, let
$s_1>0$ satisfy $s_1v\in\mathcal E_p$, and let $u\in T_pM$. Let
$\gamma:[0,s_1]\to M$, $\gamma(t):=\exp_p(tv)$ (well defined by star-shapedness
of $\mathcal E_p$), and let $J_u$ be the unique Jacobi field along
$\gamma$ with $J_u(0)=0$ and $D_tJ_u(0)=u$
([[thm-gr-jacobi-equation-and-geodesic-deviation]] clause (c),
[[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (b)). Then
$$d(\exp_p)_{tv}(tu)=J_u(t)\qquad(0\le t\le s_1);$$
in particular $d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}(s_1u)=J_u(s_1)$ and, in the special case
$s_1=1$, $v\in\mathcal E_p$, $d(\exp_p)_v(u)=J_u(1)$.

**(b) Conjugacy as a kernel condition.** With the notation of (a),
$d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}$ is injective if and only if no nonzero Jacobi field
along $\gamma$ vanishes at $t=0$ and at $t=s_1$. Moreover
$\ker d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}=s_1\{u\in T_pM:J_u(s_1)=0\}$, so
$\dim\ker d(\exp_p)_{s_1v}$ equals the multiplicity of the conjugate
instant $s_1$ whenever $\gamma(s_1)$ is conjugate to $p$ along $\gamma$
([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (d)).

**(c) Conjugate instants of a geodesic.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a smooth
geodesic with $\gamma(0)=p$, and let $s_1>0$ with $s_1\in I$ and
$s_1\gamma'(0)\in\mathcal E_p$. Then $\gamma(s_1)$ is conjugate to
$\gamma(0)=p$ along $\gamma$ if and only if $d(\exp_p)_{s_1\gamma'(0)}$ is
not injective.
items.strategy: Identify d(exp_p)_{tv}(tu) with the Jacobi field J_u(t) and characterize conjugacy as non-injectivity of the exponential differential with kernel dimension equal to the multiplicity.

items.title: The normal index form before the first conjugate instant is positive definite
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let
$a<b$ and let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a smooth future timelike geodesic with
$g(T,T)=-1$, $T:=\gamma'$, such that no instant $s\in(a,b]$ is conjugate to
$a$ along $\gamma$ ([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]]). Let
$N_\gamma$ be the normal bundle of $\gamma$ (clause (e) there) with the
positive definite fibre metric $g$, and for continuous piecewise-$C^1$
normal fields $J,K$ vanishing at $a$ and $b$ define
$$I(J,K):=\int_a^b\Bigl(g(D_sJ,D_sK)+g\bigl(R(T,J)T,K\bigr)\Bigr)ds,$$
the integral being over the smooth pieces of $J$ and $K$; write $I(J):=I(J,J)$
and $|J|:=\sqrt{g(J,J)}$.

**(a) The Jacobi operator on the normal bundle.** For every normal field $J$
the field $C_T(J):=R(T,J)T$ is again normal, and $C_T$ is $g$-selfadjoint on
each fibre: $g(C_T(J),K)=g(J,C_T(K))$ for normal fields $J,K$.

**(b) Matrix form.** Let $E_1,E_2,E_3$ be a parallel $g$-orthonormal frame of
$N_\gamma$ (which exists), and write $J=\sum_iJ^iE_i$, $K=\sum_iK^iE_i$ with
smooth coefficients on the smooth pieces. Then
$g(D_sJ,D_sK)=\sum_i(J^i)'(K^i)'$ and
$g(R(T,J)T,K)=\sum_{i,j}J^jC^i{}_jK^i$ for the smooth symmetric coefficient
functions $C^i{}_j:=g(C_T(E_j),E_i)$, so that the matrix
$C(s)=\bigl(C^i{}_j(s)\bigr)_{i,j}$ is symmetric for every $s$ and
$$I(J,K)=\int_a^b\Bigl(\textstyle\sum_i(J^i)'(K^i)'+J^TCK\Bigr)ds .$$

**(c) Factorization.** Let $A:[a,b]\to M_3(\mathbb R)$ be the unique solution
of the initial-value problem
$$A''=CA,\qquad A(a)=0,\qquad A'(a)=I_3 .$$
Then $A(s)$ is invertible for every $s\in(a,b]$, the field
$\Theta(s):=A'(s)A(s)^{-1}$ is symmetric on $(a,b]$ with
$$\Theta'=C-\Theta^2,$$
and for every continuous piecewise-$C^1$ normal field $J$ vanishing at $a$
and $b$,
$$I(J)=\int_a^b\bigl|J'-\Theta J\bigr|^2ds, $$
where $|J'-\Theta J|^2:=\sum_i\bigl((J^i)'-\sum_j\Theta^i{}_jJ^j\bigr)^2$ in
the frame of (b). Consequently $I(J)\ge0$, and $I(J)=0$ if and only if
$J=0$; the index form is positive definite on the space of such fields.
items.strategy: Show that the Jacobi operator is self-adjoint on the normal bundle, write the index form in matrix form in a parallel orthonormal frame, and factor it as a sum of squares before the first conjugate instant via the matrix Riccati equation.

items.title: Conjugacy, the exponential differential and the local proper-time maximum before the first conjugate instant
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let $b>0$ and
let $\gamma:[0,b]\to M$ be a smooth future timelike geodesic with
$g(T,T)=-1$, $T:=\gamma'$, $p:=\gamma(0)$, and suppose that no
$s\in(0,b]$ is a conjugate instant of $\gamma$ relative to $0$
([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (d)).

**(a) Conjugacy and the exponential differential.** For every $s\in(0,b]$,
$\gamma(s)$ is conjugate to $p$ along $\gamma$ if and only if
$d(\exp_p)_{sT(0)}$ is not injective; consequently
$d(\exp_p)_{sT(0)}$ is invertible for every $s\in[0,b]$.

**(b) Local proper-time maximum.** Fix a finite family of charts
$(U_1,x_1),\dots,(U_m,x_m)$ whose domains cover $\gamma([0,b])$ and a
partition $0=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ with
$\gamma([s_{i-1},s_i])\subseteq U_i$ for each $i$. For $\delta>0$ call a
piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ **$C^1$-$\delta$-close to
$\gamma$ relative to this data** when $\alpha([s_{i-1},s_i])\subseteq U_i$
for every $i$ and, on the common refinement of the admissible partitions of
$\alpha$ and $\gamma$, the coordinate representatives satisfy
$$\sup\bigl\|x_i\circ\alpha-x_i\circ\gamma\bigr\|<\delta, \qquad \sup\bigl\|(x_i\circ\alpha)'-(x_i\circ\gamma)'\bigr\|<\delta$$
on each common open piece contained in $(s_{i-1},s_i)$. Then there exists
$\delta>0$ such that every piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike curve
$\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ with $\alpha(0)=p$ and $\alpha(b)=\gamma(b)$ that is
$C^1$-$\delta$-close to $\gamma$ relative to the fixed data satisfies
$$L_g(\alpha)\le b=L_g(\gamma),$$
with equality if and only if there is a piecewise-$C^1$ strictly increasing
surjection $\rho:[0,b]\to[0,b]$ with $\alpha=\gamma\circ\rho$; that is,
$\alpha$ is a strictly monotone reparametrization of $\gamma$.

**(c) The normal index form.** The normal index form of
[[lem-gr-normal-index-form-factorization]] on the space of piecewise-$C^1$
normal fields along $\gamma$ vanishing at $0$ and $b$ is positive definite.
items.strategy: Prove invertibility of the exponential differential up to the first conjugate instant, the local proper-time maximum with its equality characterization, and positive definiteness of the normal index form.

items.title: A curvature tensor vanishes if the tidal operator vanishes for every timelike direction
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $p\in M$. Let
$R_p:(T_pM)^4\to\mathbb R$ be an **algebraic curvature tensor at $p$**: an
$\mathbb R$-multilinear map whose components $R_{abcd}$ in a basis
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]) satisfy
$$R_{abcd}=-R_{bacd}=-R_{abdc}=R_{cdab},\qquad R_{abcd}+R_{acdb}+R_{adbc}=0$$
for all $a,b,c,d$. Suppose that for every timelike $T\in T_pM$, every
$J\in T_pM$ and every $W\in T_pM$,
$$R_{abcd}W^aT^bT^cJ^d=0 .$$
Equivalently (by nondegeneracy of $g_p$), the **tidal operator**
$J\mapsto R(T,J)T$ is zero for every timelike $T$, where $R(T,J)T$ is the
vector with $g_p\bigl(R(T,J)T,W\bigr)=R_{abcd}W^aT^bT^cJ^d$ for all $W$. Then
$R_p=0$.
items.strategy: Prove that an algebraic curvature tensor at a point whose tidal operator R(T,J)T vanishes for every timelike direction is zero, by polarization of the associated symmetric bilinear forms on the spacelike hyperplanes.

items.title: Free-fall congruences, tidal (curvature) relative acceleration and the flat comparison
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] of the classical gravitational
framework, and let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and curvature
$R$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). All statements below
are deductions within the model so specified; they assert nothing about
nature.

At an event $q$, a **frame** means an ordered basis
$(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ of $T_qM$. If an orthonormal frame is intended, it means
a tetrad satisfying $g_q(E_A,E_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$;
these terms and their distinction from coordinate frames are defined in
[[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. Such a frame is pointwise basis
data, not a chart on an open set or an observer congruence, which is a smooth
future unit timelike vector field on an open set
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).

**(a) Free-fall congruences.** A **free-fall congruence** of the model is a
smooth map $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times I\to M$, with
$\varepsilon>0$ and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval with nonempty interior,
whose values we write $\gamma(r,s)$. For each
$r\in(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ the curve $\gamma_r:I\to M$ is defined by
$\gamma_r(s):=\gamma(r,s)$ and is a future timelike geodesic parametrized by
proper time, with tangent field $U_r(s):=\partial_s\gamma(r,s)$ satisfying
$$g(U_r,U_r)=-c^2,\qquad D_sU_r=0,$$
where $D_s$ is the covariant derivative along $\gamma_r$.
By clause (ii) of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]], each $\gamma_r$ is
a worldline the model assigns to an ideal freely falling massive test body
with the corresponding release data, and conversely every such worldline
arises this way on its parameter interval. No injectivity or immersion
condition is imposed on the family map.

**(b) Deviation equation (model deduction).** Let $\gamma$ be a free-fall
congruence and set $J:=\partial_r\gamma$. Then, along each $\gamma_r$, the
separation field satisfies
$$D_s^2J=R(U_r,J)U_r,$$
where $D_s$ is the covariant derivative along $\gamma_r$. In particular, the
relative four-acceleration encoded by the family’s infinitesimal separation
field $J$ is exactly the curvature term: at each event,
$J\mapsto R(U_r,J)U_r$ is an $\mathbb R$-linear map on the event's tangent
space, vanishes at $J=0$, is tensorial and independent of the frame or chart
used for its components, and contains no rest mass, charge or
internal-structure parameter of the bodies.

**(c) Flat comparison and the vanishing criterion.** If the curvature
vanishes on an open subset $O\subseteq M$, then every free-fall congruence
with worldlines in $O$ has $D_s^2J=0$ there: the model predicts no tidal
relative acceleration of freely falling test bodies in that region.
Conversely, if at an event $q$ the operator $J\mapsto R(U,J)U$ vanishes for
every future timelike $U$ and every $J\in T_qM$, then $R_q=0$; hence within
the model the tidal response of all free-fall congruences detects exactly the
curvature, and $R$ is the model's complete tidal field at every event.

**Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of the stated
postulates and the cited mathematics. No observation, apparatus, measured
input or statistical inference is used; the item contains no empirical
premises, and the word "tidal" denotes the curvature term in the model's
deviation equation, not a measured force on any particular body.
items.strategy: Derive within the adopted postulates that the deviation of free-fall congruences is exactly the curvature term R(U,J)U with no body parameters, and that vanishing curvature is equivalent to vanishing tidal response for every timelike direction.
items.physical_scope: Smooth test-field regime of the classical general-relativistic framework: a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection, ideal freely falling structureless test bodies whose worldlines are future timelike geodesics parametrized by proper time, and smooth one-parameter families of such worldlines. Excludes bodies with non-negligible self-gravity, self-force, spin, finite size or internal structure, non-geodesic motion, non-smooth or distributional matter and fields, quantum effects, and any comparison with measured data. Every conclusion is a conditional model deduction from the adopted postulates, not an observational claim.

items.title: Conventions, units and scope for curvature and tidal quantities
items.statement:
**Signs and index order.** The curvature operator, the component order and the
lowered, Ricci, scalar and Einstein contractions are fixed once in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] and used unchanged throughout
this page: $R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$ and
$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$, so that the
algebraic symmetries of [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] and the
divergence identity $\nabla^aG_{ab}=0$ of
[[thm-gr-second-bianchi-and-divergence-free-einstein]] hold in exactly the
displayed form. Sources that order the loop indices differently, or that use
the opposite overall sign, state the same mathematics in another convention;
no formula is imported from a source without converting it to this one.

**Units.** In length coordinates, in which $x^0=ct$ and all $x^a$ carry
metres and the metric components are dimensionless
([[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]), the Christoffel symbols
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have units of inverse length and the components
$R^a{}_{bcd}$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ and $S$ have units of
inverse length squared. The Einstein tensor has the same units as the Ricci
tensor, and the field-equation coupling of the framework is normalized so
that $\kappa T_{ab}$ has the same units; no numerical value of any constant
is asserted by these conventions. In other coordinates, such as charts with
an angular coordinate, individual component units change with the Jacobian
and carry no universal dimension; only invariant statements, proper times and
observer-relative quantities keep their physical reading.

**Connection artifacts versus curvature.** The Christoffel symbols are chart
functions and not tensor components; a chart can make all of them vanish at a
point ([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]) without
making the curvature vanish there:
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (c) shows
that curvature at a point is exactly the second-order metric information that
no coordinate choice can remove. Conversely a chart may have nonzero
Christoffel symbols everywhere while the curvature vanishes identically, as
for flat space in curvilinear coordinates. Curvature is also not a trace of
itself: $\operatorname{Ric}=0$ is a weaker condition than $R=0$, and the
converse implications are not asserted anywhere on this page.

**"Tidal" is a model term.** In [[pthm-gr-tidal-comparison]] the word tidal
refers to the curvature term $R(U,J)U$ in the deviation equation satisfied by
smooth free-fall congruences of the adopted model; the deduction shows that
this term is exactly the relative four-acceleration of nearby freely falling
ideal test bodies and that its vanishing for all timelike directions at an
event is equivalent to the vanishing of curvature there. It does not assert
that any real body is freely falling, that any particular measured effect is
of this form, or that agreement of any such comparison would establish the
postulates; a comparison with data would require apparatus models, empirical
premises with uncertainties and statistical inference, none of which is part
of this page.

**Scope of the maximum and conjugacy results.** The conjugacy and local
maximum statements on this page concern a single smooth geodesic segment, a
fixed exponential chart and a $C^1$-neighborhood of that segment; they assert
no global maximality, no existence of conjugate instants, and no cut-locus
classification. Global causal, completeness and singularity statements are
reserved for later pages and are not prerequisites of the results here.
items.strategy: Fix the sign, index and unit conventions of the curvature items, distinguish chart artifacts from curvature, and delimit the model status, scope and exclusions of the word tidal.

items.title: Curvature survives a first-order normal chart: an explicit metric, its normal form and its deviation field
items.statement:
On $M=\mathbb R^4$ consider the identity chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, the
metric with components
$$g_{00}=-1,\qquad g_{11}=1+(x^0)^2,\qquad g_{22}=g_{33}=1,\qquad g_{ab}=0 \ \text{for }a\neq b,$$
and the time orientation $N:=\partial_0$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected
connection and $R$ its curvature
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Then:

1. The identity chart is point-normal at the origin: $g_{ab}(0)=\eta_{ab}$,
   $\partial_ag_{bc}(0)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(0)=0$; nevertheless the
   curvature does not vanish at the origin, since
   $R_{0101}(0)=R_{1010}(0)=-1$ and $R_{0110}(0)=1$.
2. The only nonzero Christoffel symbols of the metric-selected connection are
   $$\Gamma^1{}_{10}=\Gamma^1{}_{01}=\frac{x^0}{1+(x^0)^2},\qquad \Gamma^0{}_{11}=x^0 .$$
3. The deviation equation is verified exactly on the explicit family of
   geodesics $\Phi(s,r)=(s,r,0,0)$: with $T=\partial_s\Phi$ and
   $J=\partial_r\Phi$ one has $D_s^2J=R(T,J)T$ for every $s$, and the
   relative acceleration does not vanish at the event where all connection
   symbols of the chart vanish.
items.strategy: Exhibit the metric diag(-1, 1+(x^0)^2, 1, 1), whose identity chart is point-normal at the origin with nonvanishing curvature, compute its Christoffel symbols and curvature, and verify the deviation equation on an explicit geodesic family.

items.title: A flat metric with nowhere-zero Christoffel coefficients: flat space in cylindrical coordinates
items.statement:
On the open set $\Omega:=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:x^1>0\}$ with the identity chart
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ consider the metric
$$g:=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+(x^1)^2(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2,\qquad N:=\partial_0 ,$$
and let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection and $R$ its curvature
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Writing
$X:=x^1\cos x^2$ and $Y:=x^1\sin x^2$, the chain rule gives
$dX=\cos x^2\,dx^1-x^1\sin x^2\,dx^2$ and
$dY=\sin x^2\,dx^1+x^1\cos x^2\,dx^2$, hence
$dX^2+dY^2=(dx^1)^2+(x^1)^2(dx^2)^2$: the displayed metric is the flat metric
$-(dx^0)^2+dX^2+dY^2+(dx^3)^2$ pulled back by the map
$(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)\mapsto(x^0,X,Y,x^3)$. This map is a local diffeomorphism
on all of $\Omega$, so the metric is locally the flat Minkowski metric. It is
not globally injective because $x^2\in\mathbb R$ is an unwrapped angular
coordinate; on every restriction where $x^2$ ranges over an interval of
length less than $2\pi$, it gives genuine cylindrical coordinates. The
component verification below uses only the displayed metric.

1. The only nonzero Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart are
   $$\Gamma^1{}_{22}=-x^1,\qquad \Gamma^2{}_{12}=\Gamma^2{}_{21}=\frac{1}{x^1},$$
   so these three coefficients are nonzero at every point of $\Omega$,
   while all other Christoffel symbols vanish identically.
2. The curvature vanishes identically, $R=0$, even though the chart has
   nonvanishing Christoffel symbols everywhere.
3. Consequently $R(T,J)T=0$ for every geodesic tangent $T$ and every field
   $J$ along it: for every smooth family of affinely parametrized geodesics
   the deviation equation reads $D_s^2J=0$, with no tidal term.
items.strategy: Compute the Christoffel symbols of the flat metric in cylindrical coordinates and verify, by the coordinate formula and a finite case check, that the curvature vanishes identically although no connection coefficient does.

items.title: Curvature, Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors of a metric with a round two-sphere factor
items.statement:
Let $S^2:=\{(X,Y,Z)\in\mathbb R^3:X^2+Y^2+Z^2=1\}$ with the round metric
induced by the Euclidean inner product, and let $M:=\mathbb R^2\times S^2$
with the product Lorentzian metric whose first factor has line element
$-(dx^0)^2+(dx^3)^2$. Use the sphere chart
$\sigma:(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)\to S^2$ given by
$$\sigma(\theta,\varphi)=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta),$$
and put $U:=\mathbb R^2\times\sigma((0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi))\subset M$. In the
product chart with coordinate order
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(x^0,\theta,\varphi,x^3)$, the metric is
$$g:=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+\sin^2(x^1)\,(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2,\qquad N:=\partial_0 .$$
This chart contains the equatorial geodesic segment used in
[[ex-gr-conjugate-instant-on-a-round-sphere-factor]]; the underlying manifold
has an actual $S^2$ factor, not an unwrapped angular cover. The metric is
smooth and Lorentzian on $M$ with time orientation $N$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected
connection and $R$, $R_{abcd}$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ its curvature data
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Then:

1. The only nonzero Christoffel symbols in this chart are
   $$\Gamma^1{}_{22}=-\sin x^1\cos x^1,\qquad \Gamma^2{}_{12}=\Gamma^2{}_{21}=\cot x^1 .$$
2. The curvature has exactly one independent nonzero lowered component up
   to the algebraic symmetries, namely
   $$R_{1212}=\sin^2(x^1);$$ equivalently $R(\partial_1,\partial_2)\partial_2=\sin^2(x^1)\partial_1$ and $R(\partial_1,\partial_2)\partial_1=-\partial_2$, and every component containing an index $0$ or $3$ vanishes.
3. The Ricci tensor, scalar curvature and Einstein tensor are $$\operatorname{Ric}_{11}=1,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{22}=\sin^2(x^1),\qquad S=2,\qquad G=\operatorname{diag}(1,0,0,-1).$$
4. The contracted second Bianchi identity $\nabla^aG_{ab}=0$ holds. In the
   displayed chart $U$, $\nabla_eG_{ab}=0$ identically, so the divergence
   vanishes term by term there.
items.strategy: Compute the Christoffel symbols, curvature, Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors of the product of a round unit sphere with flat time and space directions, and verify the contracted second Bianchi identity on it.

items.title: Jacobi fields in flat space are affine, and no geodesic has conjugate instants
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, the flat
Lorentzian metric $g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the time orientation
$N=\partial_0$; let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection and $R$ its
curvature ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Then:

1. In the identity chart $\nabla$ is the coordinate connection, $\Gamma\equiv0$,
   and its geodesics are exactly the affine lines $t\mapsto p+tv$; moreover
   $\exp_p(v)=p+v$ and $d(\exp_p)_u=\operatorname{id}$ for every $u\in T_pM$.
2. $R=0$: every curvature component vanishes, although the identity chart is
   global.
3. Along the geodesic $\gamma(t)=p+tv$ the covariant derivative is the
   componentwise derivative in the identity chart, and the Jacobi fields along
   $\gamma$ are exactly the affine fields
   $$J(t)=J_0+tJ_1,\qquad J_0,J_1\in\mathbb R^4 ,$$
   with $D_tJ(0)=J_1$; the space of Jacobi fields along $\gamma$ is thus the
   image of the initial-value isomorphism of
   [[thm-gr-jacobi-equation-and-geodesic-deviation]] clause (c).
4. No geodesic of this model has a conjugate instant: if
   $J(t_0)=J(t_1)=0$ for $t_0<t_1$, then $J=0$. Consistently
   $d(\exp_p)_u=\operatorname{id}$ is invertible for every $u\in T_pM$,
   because $\exp_p(v)=p+v$ is a translation.
5. For the flat congruence $F(t,r):=p+tv+rw$ with $p,v,w\in\mathbb R^4$,
   $v\neq0$, the variation field is the constant field $J=w$ and
   $D_t^2J=0=R(T,J)T$: the deviation equation holds with no curvature term,
   and the relative acceleration of the congruence vanishes identically.
items.strategy: Show that in flat space the covariant derivative is the componentwise derivative, that Jacobi fields along geodesics are exactly the affine fields J_0 + tJ_1, and that no geodesic has a conjugate instant.

items.title: An equator geodesic of the round-sphere factor: conjugate instant at distance pi with multiplicity one
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^2\times S^2$ carry the product metric of
[[ex-gr-curvature-of-a-product-with-a-round-sphere]]. Use its local chart
$U$ with $0<\theta:=x^1<\pi$, $0<\varphi:=x^2<2\pi$ and coordinate order
$(x^0,\theta,\varphi,x^3)$; this chart contains the full geodesic segment
below. The metric has time orientation $N=\partial_0$, and its Christoffel
symbols and curvature are computed in
[[ex-gr-curvature-of-a-product-with-a-round-sphere]]. Let $\nabla$ be the
metric-selected connection. Define $\gamma:[0,\pi]\to M$ and fix
$$p:=(0,\tfrac{\pi}{2},\tfrac{\pi}{2},0),\qquad \gamma(s):=(0,\tfrac{\pi}{2},\tfrac{\pi}{2}+s,0),\qquad T:=\gamma'=\partial_2 .$$
Then:

1. $\gamma$ is a geodesic with affine parameter $s$ and unit spacelike
   tangent, $g(T,T)=\sin^2(\pi/2)=1$, and every Christoffel symbol of the
   chart vanishes along $\gamma$; hence the coordinate frame
   $\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3$ is parallel along $\gamma$.
2. The smooth field $J(s):=\sin(s)\,\partial_1|_{\gamma(s)}$ along $\gamma$ is
   a nonzero Jacobi field with $J(0)=J(\pi)=0$. Therefore $\pi$ is a
   conjugate instant of $\gamma$ relative to $0$
   ([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (d)), and the events
   $p=\gamma(0)$ and $\gamma(\pi)=(0,\tfrac{\pi}{2},\tfrac{3\pi}{2},0)$ are
   distinct conjugate points of $M$.
3. No $s_1\in(0,\pi)$ is a conjugate instant of $\gamma$ relative to $0$:
   the first conjugate instant is exactly $\pi$.
4. The conjugate instant $\pi$ has multiplicity $1$, and consistently
   $\ker d(\exp_p)_{\pi T(p)}$ is the one-dimensional subspace
   $\pi\,\mathbb R\,\partial_1|_p$ of $T_pM$
   ([[lem-gr-conjugacy-via-the-exponential-map]] clause (b)).
items.strategy: Verify that the equator geodesic of the round-sphere factor has the Jacobi field sin(s) partial_1, a first conjugate instant at s = pi of multiplicity one, and a one-dimensional kernel of d(exp_p) at pi v.

items.title: The exchange symmetries of a curvature-like tensor do not imply the first Bianchi identity
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold with a global chart and
let $T$ be a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor field on $M$ whose components satisfy, at
every point,
$$T_{abcd}=-T_{bacd},\qquad T_{abcd}=-T_{abdc},\qquad T_{abcd}=T_{cdab}$$
for all $a,b,c,d$ — the skew-symmetries and the exchange of the two index
pairs of [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(b). Then $T$
also satisfies the first Bianchi identity $T_{abcd}+T_{acdb}+T_{adbc}=0$ of
clause (c)."
items.strategy: Refute the implication from the skew and pair-exchange symmetries to the first Bianchi identity with the constant tensor T_abcd = omega_ab omega_cd, whose Bianchi sum at (0,1,2,3) equals 1.

items.title: A nonzero algebraic curvature tensor whose tidal operator vanishes for one timelike direction
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "Let $R_p$ be an algebraic curvature tensor at a point $p$
of a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, with the four identities
of [[lem-gr-algebraic-curvature-vanishing-criterion]], and suppose there is
**one** timelike vector $T\in T_pM$ such that the tidal operator
$J\mapsto R(T,J)T$ vanishes for every $J\in T_pM$. Then $R_p=0$."
items.strategy: Refute the one-observer vanishing criterion with the algebraic curvature tensor R_abcd = h_ac h_bd - h_ad h_bc built from the degenerate form h, whose tidal operator vanishes for partial_0 but not for the tilted timelike direction partial_0 + (1/2) partial_1.
